title: Read a host's messages off a byte stream

cases.says: a framed message comes back as exactly the bytes the host sent, without its length
a message longer than 255 bytes uses both length bytes and comes back whole
a message whose bytes arrive over several reads is still returned whole, because one read is not one message
two messages that arrive in one read come out one per call, each with exactly its announced length
the binary length is an unsigned number, so a length byte above 127 still counts up
a stream that ends before the announced length has arrived raises EOFException instead of returning a short message
a zero-length frame is a keep-alive and is skipped, so the next real message is returned

origin.section: 3.2 One Read Is Not One Message
